rules.title: Closed issue still parked in an active stage
rules.why: The board Status is what the roadmap page and the `--auto` lane read as the stage of record. A closed issue sitting in Development makes the lane look busier than it is and hides what actually shipped — the exact drift the 2026-07-11 usage audit caught.
rules.fix: Set the board Status to Released.

rules.title: Open issue the board calls Released
rules.why: Released is a terminal stage, and under @jwildfire's one-requirement-one-release rule (2026-08-15) nothing is ever open in it on purpose. An open issue at Released is one of exactly three defects: finished work nobody closed, live work filed in the wrong lane, or a requirement whose scope spans more than one release. There is deliberately no label, marker or comment that silences this rule — an escape hatch would restore the ambiguity the rule exists to remove.
rules.fix: Close it if the work is done; move the stage back if the work is live; split it if it carries scope beyond the release it delivered.

rules.title: Board item with no Status
rules.why: An item with no Status is on the board but outside the lifecycle: it appears in no stage lane, the roadmap page has to call it "Unstaged", and the `--auto` selector cannot reason about it.
rules.fix: Set the Status the evidence supports — Released if it is closed, otherwise the stage its PRs and design artifacts imply.

rules.title: Requirement issue missing from the board
rules.why: The obot Roadmap project is the requirement tracker. A requirement that never got added is invisible to the stage lanes, to the roadmap page's stage grouping, and to any review that starts from the board — which is how a burst of promoted ideas can vanish the day after it is filed.
rules.fix: Add it to the project and give it a Status.

rules.title: Same issue on the board twice
rules.why: Duplicate items double-count a requirement in every stage tally and let two copies hold different Statuses, so the board contradicts itself. One appeared during the #53 goal migration and had to be removed by hand.
rules.fix: Remove the extra items, keeping the one that carries a Status.

rules.title: Closed parent with open sub-issues
rules.why: Sub-issues are the canonical task tracker for a requirement, so a closed parent asserts its children are finished. When they are not, the remaining work is orphaned — visible on no requirement, in no stage, and to nobody. (@jwildfire named this one as the founding example of the audit.)
rules.fix: Close the children that are actually done; move genuine follow-on scope to a follow-up requirement — the #30 → #88 precedent — or reopen the parent.

rules.title: All sub-issues closed, parent still open
rules.why: When every task under a requirement is closed the requirement is done being built; leaving it open in an earlier stage means the board understates progress and the review queue never surfaces it.
rules.fix: Move it to Review, or close it if it has already sat in Review.

rules.title: Open requirement under no goal
rules.why: Since #53 goals are hub issues and membership is the sub-issue link — nothing else. Membership is inherited, so a requirement nested under another requirement still belongs to that requirement’s goal; only an issue with no goal anywhere up its parent chain belongs to no standing direction, never appears on a goal page, and can never be picked up by an autonomous session selecting by goal.
rules.fix: Link it under the goal it serves, or state why it is deliberately standalone.

rules.title: Hub issue in no structure at all
rules.why: The hub has exactly three ways an issue is visible: the `requirement` label puts it on the roadmap page, a sub-issue link puts it on a goal page, and a board item puts it in a stage lane. An issue with none of the three is filed and then invisible — it will be found again only by accident.
rules.fix: Link it under the goal or requirement it belongs to, or promote it to a requirement.

rules.title: Goal with no member requirements
rules.why: A goal exists to group work and to give an autonomous session something to select from. With no sub-issues it is a statement of intent the machinery cannot act on.
rules.fix: Link the requirements that serve it, or retire the goal.

rules.title: Goals inconsistently placed on the board
rules.why: Goals are permanent and do not move through the requirement stages, so a goal on the delivery board is an item with no stage it can ever reach. @jwildfire settled the convention on 2026-08-15 (audit decision R3-a): goals are not board items. They are surfaced by the goal pages and the hierarchy view, which are the better surfaces for something that never finishes.
rules.fix: Take the goal off the board. Nothing is deleted — the goal issue and its sub-issue links are untouched.

rules.title: Merged PR whose closing target is still open
rules.why: GitHub only auto-closes an issue when the PR is in the same repository. Cross-repo `Closes` lines — the norm here, where implementation PRs live in spoke repos and requirements live in the hub — merge silently without closing anything.
rules.fix: Close the referenced issue.

rules.title: Open PR against an already-closed issue
rules.why: Either the branch is stale work that should be dropped, or the issue was closed while its implementation was still in review. Both are worth knowing; neither resolves itself.
rules.fix: Close the PR, or reopen the issue.

rules.title: Open PR with no requirement link
rules.why: The Issue–PR Link Convention exists so a merge closes its requirement and the roadmap page can show which requirement a PR is moving. An unlinked PR is invisible to both.
rules.fix: Add the closing reference to the requirement or task it implements.

rules.title: Requirement-titled issue without the `requirement` label
rules.why: Every generator selects requirements by label. An issue titled "Requirement: …" without the label is absent from the roadmap page, the stage tallies and the goal pages — present on GitHub, missing from the project.
rules.fix: Add the `requirement` label.

rules.title: Tracked issue with no assignee
rules.why: The Assignee Convention puts @jwildfire on every issue the agent files, so his GitHub views ("assigned to me") are the same working set the roadmap shows. Unassigned issues fall out of that view.
rules.fix: Assign @jwildfire.

rules.title: Open requirement with no milestone
rules.why: Milestones are the delivery slot (`backlog`, `2026q3`, `2026q4`) and drive the release-facing views. A requirement with none is unscheduled by omission rather than by decision.
rules.fix: Set `backlog` for anything not yet scheduled; pick the quarter for work in flight.

rules.title: Requirement past Design with no design
rules.why: The lifecycle puts Design before Development for a reason: sub-issues are supposed to be decomposed from it. A requirement in Development whose Design section is empty or "TBD" means the decomposition was improvised, and there is nothing for a reviewer or an autonomous session to work from.
rules.fix: Populate the Design section, or add a design doc under requirements/design/.

rules.title: Issue labelled both `auto` and `draft`
rules.why: The two labels are opposites: `auto` means the #18 implementation-ready criteria are met and an autonomous session may take it; `draft` means it needs @jwildfire's steering first. Carrying both means the `--auto` selector may pick up work that was explicitly gated.
rules.fix: Keep whichever the issue actually satisfies and drop the other.

rules.title: Issue body hard-wrapped mid-paragraph
rules.why: GitHub renders a single newline as a line break, so a body wrapped at 80 columns arrives as ragged half-lines. @jwildfire's standing instruction is one line per paragraph or bullet in anything posted to GitHub.
rules.fix: Rewrap the body to one line per paragraph.

rules.title: Promoted idea thread still open
rules.why: Triage closes a thread as resolved when it becomes an issue; that closure is what keeps the Ideas board an inbox rather than an archive. A promoted thread left open keeps showing up as un-triaged work.
rules.fix: Close the discussion as resolved.

rules.title: In-flight requirement that stopped moving
rules.why: Development and Review are lanes for work happening now. A requirement that has not been touched in two weeks, with no open PR behind it, is parked — and while it sits in an active lane it crowds out the real front line on every view of the roadmap.
rules.fix: Park it back at Backlog. Dragging it forward on the board is how you say it is live again.

subject.title: Requirement: R/Pharma 2026 developer-diary blog series

evidence: three or more consecutive wrapped lines outside a list, table or code fence

proposal.summary: Rewrap the body to one line per paragraph, changing no wording.
proposal.prompt: Read the issue body. Join hard-wrapped paragraph lines into one line each, leaving lists, tables, code fences and HTML comments untouched. Change no wording, no headings and no content — this is whitespace only. Update the body via the REST API. If the body turns out not to be hard-wrapped (the detection is heuristic), do nothing and say so.
